title: How To Implement Google's Responsive Search Ads - Ten Thousand Foot View

facts.fact: Responsive Search Ads offer up to 3 headlines and 2 description texts, compared with Expanded Text Ads' 2 headlines and 1 description text.
facts.quote: this new ad format offers up to 3 headlines and 2 description texts compared with Expanded Text Ads’ (ETAs) 2 headlines and 1 description text.

facts.fact: Responsive Search Ads offer 90% more text than Expanded Text Ads, according to the author.
facts.quote: That’s 90% more text available in your search ads!

facts.fact: An RSA can contain up to 15 different headlines.
facts.quote: you can create up to 15 different headlines and 4 different descriptions.

facts.fact: Google claims that ad groups with Responsive Search Ads generate between 5-15% more clicks on average.
facts.quote: Google claims that ad groups with RSAs generate between 5-15% more clicks on average.

facts.fact: Google recommends against using Responsive Search Ads in branded ad groups.
facts.quote: Google recommends against using RSAs in branded ad groups.

facts.fact: The author recommends creating at least 5 headlines for an RSA, as Google recommends, because 3 headlines would mean running the same headlines repeatedly.
facts.quote: Google recommends creating at least 5 headlines, which makes sense, since having only 3 means running the same headlines over and over

facts.fact: Creating a new RSA in the Google Ads editor initially presents 5 headlines and 2 description texts.
facts.quote: Instead of 2 headlines and 1 description text you’ll be presented with 5 headlines and 2 description texts.

facts.fact: Google rolled out the ability to view impressions by asset (ad copy snippet) and by combination for RSAs shortly before the article was published.
facts.quote: Just this past week, Google did roll out the ability to view impressions by asset (ad copy snippet) as well as impressions by combination (complete ad units).
